title: Cylinders over countably m-rectifiable sets are countably (m+1)-rectifiable
statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, Hᵏ := μHE[k] and π(y) := (y_1, …, y_P) for y ∈ ℝ^{P+1} (Lean: (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ y))). Assume (NT): for every N ⊆ ℝ^P with Hᵐ(N) = 0, H^{m+1}({y : π(y) ∈ N}) = 0. If M ⊆ ℝ^P is countably m-rectifiable (Simon Ch. 3, 1.1: M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^m) with Hᵐ(M₀) = 0 and F_j : ℝ^m → ℝ^P Lipschitz), then the cylinder {y ∈ ℝ^{P+1} : π(y) ∈ M} is countably (m+1)-rectifiable.
lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ), (∀ N : Set (Eucl P), (μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P)) N = 0 → (μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl (P + 1))) {y | (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y)) ∈ N} = 0) → ∀ M : Set (Eucl P), CountablyRectifiable m M → CountablyRectifiable (m + 1) {y : Eucl (P + 1) | (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y)) ∈ M}
